title_en: Shao Ping v. Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the determination of legal liability for abuse of corporate personality and limited liability shall be made by comprehensively considering various factors. In practice, factors such as the background of the company's establishment, the status of the company's shareholders, controllers, and principal financial personnel, the company's main business operations and the purpose of transactions between the company and other companies, the company's tax payment situation, as well as the background circumstances and performance status when a specific creditor entered into a contract with the company, shall all be included in the scope of consideration.

full_text_en:
Shao Ping v. Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 20 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the determination of a company's legal liability for abuse of corporate personality and limited liability shall be made by synthesizing multiple factors. In practice, factors such as the background of the company's establishment, the circumstances of the company's shareholders, controllers, and principal financial personnel, the company's main business operations and the purpose of transactions between the company and other companies, the company's tax payment status, and the background and performance circumstances when a specific creditor entered into a contract with the company, shall all be included in the scope of examination.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 260

Appellant (plaintiff of the first instance): Shao Ping, female, Han ethnicity, born on June 28, 1962, residing at Room 301, Unit 3, Building 164, Group 10, Xinying Residential Community, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.

Agent ad litem: Huang Wei, lawyer of Yunnan Tianzhitai Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant of the first instance): Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Lishan Ma'anshan, Tonghai County, Yuxi City, Yunnan Province.

Legal representative: Yue Yue, general manager of the company.

Respondent (defendant of the first instance): Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Lishan Ma'anshan, Tonghai County, Yuxi City, Yunnan Province.

Legal representative: Chen Jianming, chairman of the board of directors of the company.

With respect to the dispute over private lending between the appellant Shao Ping and the respondents Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kuntong Company) and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xingtongda Company), the High People's Court of Yunnan Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance or Yunnan High Court) rendered a civil judgment (2011) Yun Gao Min Yi Chu Zi No. 4 on December 15, 2012, which has become legally effective. Shao Ping, dissatisfied with that judgment, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 1691 on November 26, 2013, instructing Yunnan High Court to retry the case. Yunnan High Court rendered a civil judgment (2014) Yun Gao Min Zai Chu Zi No. 1 on May 18, 2015. Shao Ping, dissatisfied with that judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on December 3, 2015. Shao Ping and her agent ad litem Huang Wei, and the legal representative of Xingtongda Company, Chen Jianming, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Kuntong Company was served with a summons but did not appear in court. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

1. On March 29, 2011, Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company entered into a "Loan Agreement," stipulating that Xingtongda Company would borrow RMB 29.2 million from Shao Ping, with a loan term of 12 months, interest at the loan rate of the same period of the bank, and repayment of principal and interest upon maturity. Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company, signed the agreement. The performance of the above-mentioned amounts is as follows:
   (1) On August 29, 2009, Shao Ping transferred RMB 1 million to Chen Jianming's account.
   (2) On February 9, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Lihua to remit RMB 1 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (3) On April 1, 2010, Shao Ping paid RMB 4 million in cash to Xingtongda Company. At the same time, Kuntong Company issued a "Guarantee Letter" to Shao Ping, promising that Kuntong Company would assume joint and several liability for the loan from Xingtongda Company to Shao Ping.
   (4) On June 3, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Haoxue to remit RMB 2 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (5) On June 3, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Chen Yu to remit RMB 2 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (6) On June 3, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Mou Shanlan to remit RMB 2 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (7) On June 4, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Li Jie to remit RMB 1.75 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (8) On June 4, 2010, Shao Ping paid RMB 250,000 in cash to Chen Jianming.
   (9) On June 8, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Mou Shanlan to remit RMB 2 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (10) On July 5, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Mou Shanlan to remit RMB 8.08 million to Chen Jianming's account.
   (11) On July 5, 2010, Shao Ping paid RMB 920,000 in cash to Chen Jianming.
   (12) On August 30, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Lihua to transfer RMB 2 million to Chen Jianming's account.
   (13) On August 31, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Haoxue to remit RMB 1.9 million to Chen Jianming's account.
   (14) On September 16, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Zhu Zhengying to remit RMB 300,000 to Chen Jianming's account.

2. On March 29, 2011, Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company entered into a "Loan Agreement," stipulating that Xingtongda Company would borrow RMB 17.16 million from Shao Ping, with a loan term of 12 months, interest at the loan rate of the same period of the bank. Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company, signed the agreement. The performance is as follows:
   (1) On June 19, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Mou Shanlan to transfer RMB 1 million to Chen Jianming.
   (2) On July 17, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 1.4 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (3) On August 18, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 500,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (4) On September 1, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Lihua to remit RMB 900,000 to Chen Jianming.
   (5) On October 19, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Haoxue to remit RMB 600,000 to Chen Jianming.
   (6) On December 3, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 150,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (7) On December 8, 2009, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 219,600 to Xingtongda Company.
   (8) On February 9, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 300,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (9) On February 9, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 500,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (10) On March 22, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Co., Ltd. to endorse and transfer a bank acceptance draft of RMB 500,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (11) On November 15, 2010, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Haoxue to remit RMB 1.65 million to Chen Jianming.
   (12) On April 18, 2011, Shao Ping remitted RMB 4,040,960 to Xingtongda Company.
   (13) On April 21, 2011, Shao Ping paid RMB 1 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (14) On April 21, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Shao Haoxue to remit RMB 1 million to Chen Jianming.
   (15) On April 22, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Zhu Zhengying to remit RMB 800,000 to Xingtongda Company.
   (16) On September 15, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Shengshi Wuyu Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. to pay RMB 1 million to Xingtongda Company.
   (17) On September 16, 2011, Shao Ping delivered RMB 700,000 in cash to Chen Jianming.
   (18) On September 16, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Yunnan Shengshi Wuyu Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. to pay RMB 1 million to Xingtongda Company.

The total amount of the above 18 payments is RMB 17,332,560, which is RMB 172,560 more than the loan amount of RMB 17.16 million stated in the Loan Agreement.

3. On March 18, 2011, Xingtongda Company issued a "Receipt" to Shao Ping, stating that Xingtongda Company had received cash of RMB 4.905 million borrowed from Shao Ping, bearing the seal of Xingtongda Company and the signature of its legal representative Chen Jianming, and the signature of Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company.

4. On October 10, 2011, Xingtongda Company issued a "Receipt for Payment" to Shao Ping, stating that Xingtongda Company had received a loan of RMB 18.895 million from Shao Ping, bearing the seal of Xingtongda Company and the signature of its legal representative Chen Jianming, and the signature of Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company. The performance is as follows:
   (1) On June 8, 2011, Shao Ping, at the request of Xingtongda Company, paid RMB 1.2 million in cash to Ma Yukun on behalf of Xingtongda Company.
   (2) On June 24, 2011, Shao Ping transferred RMB 1.5 million through bank to Chen Jianming.
   (3) On May 23, 2011, Shao Ping, at the request of Xingtongda Company, remitted RMB 2 million through Sichuan Shenghui Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. to Kunming Huashengyuan Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huashengyuan Company). For the remaining amounts, from February 25, 2011 to May 24, 2011, Shao Ping entrusted Zhu Zhengying, Jinning Kunyang Fengqiong Minerals Business Department, Sichuan Shenghui Construction and Installation Engineering Co., Ltd. to remit and endorsed and transferred bank acceptance drafts from Jinning County Erjie Township Laogao Mineral Powder Factory, Yunnan Phosphate Chemical Group Sales Co., Ltd., etc. to Xingtongda Company.

5. On September 28, 2011, Zhao Guangzhou lent RMB 2 million to Xingtongda Company. On October 10, 2011, Xingtongda Company issued a "Receipt for Payment" for receiving the RMB 2 million loan to Zhao Guangzhou, which bore the seal of Xingtongda Company and the signature of its legal representative Chen Jianming, and the signature of Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company. On October 28, 2011, Zhao Guangzhou issued a "Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights," assigning the RMB 2 million claim to Shao Ping.

6. On February 1, 2011, Xingtongda Company issued two "Receipts" to Chen Jianhua, stating that Xingtongda Company had received RMB 2 million in loans from Chen Jianhua. On October 28, 2011, Chen Jianhua issued a "Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights," assigning the RMB 2 million claim to Shao Ping.

7. On October 17, 2011, after reconciliation between Xingtongda Company and Huashengyuan Company, a "Confirmation Letter of Reconciliation" was formed, stating that as of October 17, 2011, Xingtongda Company owed Huashengyuan Company RMB 32,568,125.44 (including RMB 27,568,125.44 for goods and RMB 5 million for loans). On October 28, 2011, Huashengyuan Company issued a "Notice of Assignment of Creditor's Rights," assigning the RMB 32,568,125.44 claim to Shao Ping.

The court of first instance further found: Xingtongda Company was established on September 14, 2009, with its legal representative being Chen Jianming, and its shareholders being Chen Jianming, Yue Xian, and Huang Yun. The legal representative of Kuntong Company is Yue Yue, and its shareholders are Yue Xiukuan and Zhang Shufen.

In November 2011, Shao Ping filed a lawsuit against Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company in the court of first instance, requesting a judgment: 1. That Kuntong Company immediately repay Shao Ping the principal of the creditor's rights totaling RMB 106,728,125.44 and interest (calculated at the bank loan rate of the same period until the date of full repayment of the principal; as of November 1, 2011, the interest was RMB 1,774,042.67); 2. That Kuntong Company's property be given priority to satisfy all of Shao Ping's creditor's rights principal and interest; 3. That Xingtongda Company assume joint and several liability; 4. That all litigation costs of this case be borne by Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company.

Kuntong Company argued in its defense that Kuntong Company was not a proper defendant in this case, that Kuntong Company had not entered into any loan contract with Shao Ping, and that Shao Ping's request for Kuntong Company to assume repayment obligations had no legal basis. Therefore, it requested that Shao Ping's claims be dismissed.

Xingtongda Company argued in its defense that the purpose of Xingtongda Company's establishment was to accept the entrustment of Kuntong Company, and that Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company had an agency relationship. Xingtongda Company, in its own name, represented Kuntong Company in entering into loan relationships with Shao Ping. The legal representative of Kuntong Company signed the main loan documents and loan contracts, and all the funds involved were used entirely for Kuntong Company's equipment maintenance and production operations. After verification with Shao Ping, Xingtongda Company had no objection to the transaction vouchers and loan amounts submitted by Shao Ping. Therefore, it requested that Kuntong Company be ordered to assume the repayment liability.

The court of first instance held that the issues in dispute in this case were: first, who was the borrower; second, how to calculate the loan principal and interest.

I. Regarding the issue of who was the borrower

First, from the evidence submitted by Shao Ping, the counterparty to the loan contract was Xingtongda Company, and the actual recipient was also Xingtongda Company and its legal representative Chen Jianming. Second, upon the application of Xingtongda Company, the court of first instance obtained from the Tonghai County State Tax Bureau and Xiushan Branch the originals of the "Report on the Production and Operation Status of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" dated September 16, 2009, and the "Report on the Reasons for the Formation of the Tax Burden Status of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" dated October 25, 2011. These documents could only prove the existence of a purchase and sale relationship of raw materials and products between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company, and could not prove that Xingtongda Company was the agent of Kuntong Company, borrowing money from Shao Ping under the entrustment of Kuntong Company. Third, the signature of Yue Yue on the two "Loan Agreements," "Receipts," and "Receipts for Payment" was merely an act of witnessing and could not be regarded as Kuntong Company borrowing money from Shao Ping, or Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company jointly borrowing money from Shao Ping. Fourth, the "Guarantee Letter" dated June 3, 2010, submitted by Shao Ping, was a guarantee provided by Kuntong Company for Xingtongda Company's borrowing from a third party, Shao Haoxue, and was not a guarantee for the loan in this case. This "Guarantee Letter" was not relevant to this case. Although Kuntong Company, in the "Guarantee Letter" dated April 1, 2010, promised to provide joint and several guarantee for Xingtongda Company's borrowing of RMB 4 million from Shao Ping, the term of that loan was from April 1, 2010 to December 1, 2010. By the time Shao Ping filed this lawsuit on November 8, 2011, the six-month guarantee period had expired. Shao Ping's assertion that Xingtongda Company was the agent of Kuntong Company, acting as agent for Kuntong Company in borrowing from Shao Ping, was not supported by sufficient evidence. The borrower of the funds claimed by Shao Ping was Xingtongda Company, and the repayment liability should be borne by Xingtongda Company. Kuntong Company shall not bear repayment liability in this case.

II. Regarding the issue of loan principal and interest

The loan amount claimed by Shao Ping was RMB 106,728,125.44, which was acknowledged by Xingtongda Company. However, among this amount, RMB 32,568,125.44 was a claim for the price of goods owed by Xingtongda Company to a third party, Huashengyuan Company, which Shao Ping had acquired by assignment. This did not fall within the same legal relationship as the private lending in this case. Therefore, this amount of goods price was not included for handling in this case; Shao Ping may pursue it separately. The principal of the loan to be repaid by Xingtongda Company to Shao Ping was RMB 74.16 million (RMB 106,728,125.44 - RMB 32,568,125.44). Regarding interest, it should be calculated in stages. First, there were 23 payments made before March 29, 2011, totaling RMB 34,791,600. Since Shao Ping waived claiming interest for the period before the agreement was signed, the interest for this portion shall be calculated from the date the agreement was signed to the day before the filing of this case. Second, the remaining 9 payments totaling RMB 11,568,400 were delivered successively after March 29, 2011. The interest for each loan shall be calculated from the day after the delivery date. However, because the actual amount delivered was RMB 17,332,560, which was RMB 172,560 more than the agreed amount, and Shao Ping claimed interest based on the agreed amount of RMB 17.16 million, the principal for calculating interest for the last payment of RMB 1 million on September 16, 2011, should be reduced to RMB 827,440. As for the other 4 payments totaling RMB 27.8 million, since no loan term or payment of interest was agreed upon, interest shall be calculated from the date of filing of this case.

Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Xingtongda Company shall, within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment, repay Shao Ping the loan principal of RMB 74.16 million; 2. Xingtongda Company shall, within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment, repay Shao Ping interest on the loan principal of RMB 74.16 million (specifically: (1) interest on the principal of RMB 34,791,600, calculated from March 29, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (2) interest on the principal of RMB 4,040,960, calculated from April 19, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (3) interest on the principal of RMB 2 million, calculated from April 22, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (4) interest on the principal of RMB 800,000, calculated from April 23, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (5) interest on the principal of RMB 1.9 million, calculated from September 1, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (6) interest on the principal of RMB 1 million, calculated from September 16, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (7) interest on the principal of RMB 827,440, calculated from September 17, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (8) interest on the principal of RMB 74.16 million, calculated from November 8, 2011 until the expiration of the performance period specified in this judgment), at the loan interest rate of the same period of the People's Bank of China; 3. Shao Ping's other claims were dismissed. The case acceptance fee was RMB 584,310.84, of which Shao Ping was to bear RMB 178,214.81, and Xingtongda Company was to bear RMB 406,096.03.

Shao Ping's request for retrial was to set aside the original judgment and amend the judgment to support all her claims. The main reasons were: 1. The focus of dispute in this case should be which party should bear the repayment liability for Shao Ping's creditor's rights. 2. The legal representative of Kuntong Company, Yue Yue, signed the "Loan Agreement" for RMB 29.2 million on March 29, 2011, the "Loan Agreement" for RMB 17.16 million, the "Receipt" for RMB 4.905 million on April 18, 2011, the "Receipt for Payment" for RMB 18.895 million on October 10, 2011, and the "Receipt for Payment" for RMB 2 million from Zhao Guangzhou on October 10, 2011. Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company should jointly bear the liability for compensation to Shao Ping. 3. Regarding the "Guarantee Letter" issued by Kuntong Company on June 3, 2010, the Shao Haoxue mentioned in the guarantee was Shao Ping's daughter and agent. This guarantee letter directly binds Shao Ping and Kuntong Company. 4. The purpose of Xingtongda Company's establishment was to handle all business operations for Kuntong Company under its entrustment. Therefore, the contractual relationship between Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company directly binds the principal Kuntong Company and the third party Shao Ping. 5. The court of first instance did not grant Xingtongda Company's application for auditing Xingtongda Company's financial receipts and expenditures since September 2009, and thus failed to determine that Kuntong Company was the true user and beneficiary of the funds involved in this case, which was procedurally illegal. 6. The claim of RMB 32,568,125.44 that Shao Ping acquired by assignment from Huashengyuan Company should not be handled in a separate case.

Xingtongda Company had no objection to the amount of the creditor's rights claimed by Shao Ping, and no objection to Shao Ping's request for retrial and the reasons therefor. However, it emphasized that Xingtongda Company was merely an agent of Kuntong Company, and Kuntong Company was the true debtor in this case, so the judgment should be amended to have Kuntong Company bear the debt in this case.

Kuntong Company did not appear in court for the retrial to participate in the proceedings or to defend.

Because Xingtongda Company, in the first instance and the retrial, acknowledged Shao Ping's claim that she had acquired creditor's rights of RMB 106,728,125.44 against Xingtongda Company by lending to Xingtongda Company and by acquiring claims against Xingtongda Company from others, Yunnan High Court confirmed in the retrial that Shao Ping held creditor's rights of RMB 106,728,125.44 against Xingtongda Company.

After review, the court of first instance in retrial determined that the focus of the retrial dispute was whether Xingtongda Company was the agent of Kuntong Company and whether the creditor's rights claimed by Shao Ping should be repaid by Kuntong Company.

The court of first instance in retrial held that: First, the evidence provided by Shao Ping was insufficient to prove that the purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to handle all business activities for Kuntong Company, that Xingtongda Company was the agent of Kuntong Company, and that Xingtongda Company, in its own name, borrowed funds from Shao Ping, Zhao Guangzhou, and Chen Jianhua, and settled transactions with Huachengyuan Company, all of which were done upon the entrustment of Kuntong Company and on behalf of Kuntong Company. The reasons are as follows: 1. From the evidence submitted by Shao Ping, all the loan contracts involved were signed by Xingtongda Company and Shao Ping, and the actual recipients were also Xingtongda Company and its legal representative, Chen Jianming. 2. There was no agency agreement between Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company. Kuntong Company only acknowledged a business cooperation relationship with Xingtongda Company and denied any agency relationship. 3. According to the "Minutes of the Creditors' Meeting Involving Tonghai Kuntong Industry and Trade Company" dated June 10, 2009, obtained by the court of first instance from the Enforcement Division of Yuxi Intermediate People's Court, Kuntong Company's assets were handed over to Huachengyuan Company for management, and its debts were to be assisted in performance by Huachengyuan Company, not as Shao Ping claimed, that Xingtongda Company was established to handle all business activities for Kuntong Company and act as its agent to raise funds. 4. From the originals of the "Report on the Production and Operation of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" dated September 16, 2009, and the "Report on the Causes of Tax Burden of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" dated October 25, 2011, submitted by Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company to Tonghai County State Tax Bureau and Xiushan Branch, obtained by the court of first instance upon the application of Xingtongda Company, there was no statement that "Although Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company are two entities, all their business activities are integrated, and all external business activities of Xingtongda Company are conducted on behalf of and in service of Kuntong Company, and are all business activities of Kuntong Company," or "Xingtongda Company is the business agent of Kuntong Company," or "All business of Kuntong Company is conducted in the name of Xingtongda Company." The statement that Xingtongda Company's "procurement and sales for Kuntong Company adopt the following methods: 1. Raw materials are purchased and sold at cost; 2. A minimal purchase-sales margin is retained on product sales (to cover Xingtongda Company's daily basic expenses)" does not prove an agency relationship between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company.

Second, although Yue Yue signed the 29.2 million yuan Loan Agreement of March 29, 2011, the 17.16 million yuan Loan Agreement, the receipt for 4.905 million yuan of April 18, 2011, the receipt for 18.895 million yuan of October 10, 2011, and the receipt for 2 million yuan of Zhao Guangzhou of October 10, 2011, these loan agreements and receipts clearly indicate that the borrower was Xingtongda Company, not Kuntong Company or Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company together. Moreover, Yue Yue did not indicate that he was signing on behalf of Kuntong Company as a borrower. In the absence of other evidence proving that Xingtongda Company was acting as Kuntong Company's agent in borrowing from Shao Ping, Kuntong Company cannot be deemed the actual borrower or co-borrower of these funds.

As to whether Kuntong Company was a guarantor for these loans. Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning Guarantees in Economic Contract Disputes" states: "If a guarantor signs or seals on the main contract, which contains a guarantee clause, between the creditor and the guaranteed party in the capacity of a guarantor; or if the main contract contains no guarantee clause, but the guarantor signs or seals on the main contract in the capacity of a guarantor, the guarantee contract is deemed established." In this case, the above loan agreements and receipts contained no guarantee stipulations, and Yue Yue did not indicate that he was signing on behalf of Kuntong Company in the capacity of a guarantor. Yue Yue's signature did not meet the legal and judicial interpretation requirements for the formation of a guarantee contract, and it cannot be deemed that Yue Yue, on behalf of Kuntong Company, provided a guarantee for these debts. The original judgment's characterization of Yue Yue's signature as an attestation act was not improper.

Third, the "Guarantee Letter" issued by Kuntong Company on June 3, 2010, was a promise by Kuntong Company to provide joint and several liability guarantees with its assets, products, and by-products for Xingtongda Company's loans from Shao Haoxue, not for loans from Shao Ping to Xingtongda Company. This Guarantee Letter is irrelevant to this case. Moreover, the Guarantee Letter did not specify the guaranteed amount or term. The funds lent by Shao Haoxue to Xingtongda Company constituted only a small portion of the total creditor's rights claimed by Shao Ping. Even if Shao Haoxue was Shao Ping's agent, the Guarantee Letter could not have the legal effect of binding all creditor's rights between Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company. Shao Ping cannot rely on it to require Kuntong Company to assume guarantee liability for all her creditor's rights. Furthermore, Shao Ping's request in this regard contradicted her claim in this lawsuit that Kuntong Company should bear direct repayment liability.

Fourth, agency is a legal relationship. Whether an agency relationship exists between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company must be determined based on legal provisions and the entrustment relationship between the parties. There is no necessary connection between the economic dealings between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company and whether an agency relationship exists between them. Even if the economic dealings between the two companies were ascertained, it would not prove the existence of an agency relationship. Appraising the economic dealings between the two companies would not help resolve the dispute in this case. Therefore, the original trial's refusal to grant Xingtongda Company's application for an appraisal of the dealings between it and Kuntong Company was not improper.

Fifth, this case, in which Shao Ping sued, is a dispute over private lending, whereas the 32,568,125.44 yuan creditor's right that Shao Ping acquired from Huachengyuan Company against Xingtongda Company arises from a goods sales dispute, which is not a dispute of the same nature. Therefore, the original judgment's decision not to include that part of the creditor's right in this case and to require Shao Ping to file a separate lawsuit was not improper.

In conclusion, the claims by Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company that Xingtongda Company was Kuntong Company's agent and that Xingtongda Company borrowed from Shao Ping on behalf of Kuntong Company cannot be established. The existing evidence in this case only proves that Xingtongda Company is the debtor of the creditor's rights claimed by Shao Ping, and Shao Ping's creditor's rights should be repaid by Xingtongda Company. The court of first instance held that the original judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be affirmed. Shao Ping's retrial request could not be established. Accordingly, after deliberation by the judicial committee of the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 207, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered judgment affirming the (2011) Yunnan Civil First Instance No. 4 Civil Judgment. The retrial case acceptance fee of 584,310.84 yuan shall be borne by Shao Ping.

Shao Ping, dissatisfied with the retrial judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing: First, Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company were mixed in terms of personnel, operations, and property, and should be deemed to have corporate personality confusion. According to Article 20, Paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the two companies should bear joint and several liability. The retrial judgment found the facts incorrectly. Second, the signature of Yue Yue, the legal representative of Kuntong Company, on the loan agreements constituted Kuntong Company's confirmation of the debts, and Kuntong Company should bear joint and several liability with Xingtongda Company. Third, the Guarantee Letter issued by Kuntong Company on June 3, 2010, was a guarantee for the loans made by Xingtongda Company from Shao Ping. Shao Haoxue was Shao Ping's agent, and the Guarantee Letter directly bound Kuntong Company and Shao Ping. The retrial judgment's finding that it was a guarantee for loans from Shao Haoxue was erroneous. Fourth, the 32,568,125.44 yuan creditor's right against Xingtongda Company that Shao Ping acquired from Huachengyuan Company should be resolved together in this case. Fifth, the court of first instance failed to conduct a financial audit of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company as requested by Shao Ping, and failed to ascertain the fund flows between the two companies, which was a procedural error. In conclusion, Shao Ping requested: 1. Revocation of the (2014) Yunnan High People's Court Civil Retrial First Instance No. 1 Civil Judgment and the (2011) Yunnan High People's Court Civil First Instance No. 4 Civil Judgment. 2. Judgment in favor of Shao Ping's claims in the first instance.

During the second instance trial, Shao Ping's side confirmed that it had no objection to the amount of creditor's rights and the method of calculating interest as determined by the Yunnan High People's Court in the retrial. Regarding the creditor's rights it had acquired from Huachengyuan Company, it requested this Court to render a judgment together in this case.

Xingtongda Company argued in its defense: It had no objection to the amount of Shao Ping's creditor's rights and the method of calculating interest as determined by the Yunnan High People's Court in the retrial, but the actual borrower of this debt was Kuntong Company. There existed the fact of personality confusion between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company as alleged by Shao Ping. Xingtongda Company was established to solve problems such as Kuntong Company's assets and accounts being frozen by the people's court, and its tax control device being seized by the tax authority, which prevented it from operating. The two companies had the same financial personnel, maintained separate accounts, and were managed uniformly, with the purpose of revitalizing Kuntong Company to achieve profitability and repay its creditors. Xingtongda Company engaged in the same business activities as Kuntong Company, and with the approval of the tax authorities, its taxation was conducted on a cost-to-cost basis. All funds raised were used for Kuntong Company's equipment upgrades, production, and debt repayment. Therefore, Xingtongda Company was Kuntong Company's agent. The signature of Yue Yue, Kuntong Company's legal representative, on the loan contracts and guarantee letters in question should be construed as Kuntong Company's intention to assume all debts. The Yunnan High People's Court's characterization of this act as an attestation was erroneous.

Kuntong Company did not submit a defense during the second instance.

In addition to the facts found by the Yunnan High People's Court in the first instance, Shao Ping applied during the second instance of this Court for the witnesses Zhu Yao, a shareholder of Huachengyuan Company, and Chen Jianhua, the chairman of Huachengyuan Company, to testify in court. Both witnesses stated during the trial that due to the debts owed by Kuntong Company being enforced by the court, and in order to revitalize Kuntong Company's assets to generate profits for debt repayment, a creditors' meeting was held at the Yuxi Intermediate People's Court, where minutes were reached for Huachengyuan Company to take over operations. Later, Kuntong Company itself established Xingtongda Company as a platform for Kuntong Company's external operations and financing. After Xingtongda Company was established, Huachengyuan Company sold coke to Kuntong Company through Xingtongda Company. Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company had one set of personnel and two separate business licenses; Xingtongda Company had neither production equipment nor production conditions. Xingtongda Company considered the statements of the two witnesses to be consistent with the facts.

During the second instance trial, Shao Ping submitted the following new evidence:

1. The "Agreed Agreement" signed by Yue Xian and Kuntong Company on August 30, 2009, the main content of which was that to initiate the operation of Xingtongda Company, Yue Xian, on behalf of Kuntong Company, would jointly establish and operate Xingtongda Company with Chen Jianming as an individual shareholder, but the rights and obligations of the shareholders would be borne by Kuntong Company. This agreement was derived from the WeChat conversations and photos between Shao Ping and Yue Xian on October 7 and October 10, 2015.

2. A query slip for the mobile phone number registered under Yue Xian's name, obtained from China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., Qujing Branch. It was verified in court that the WeChat account was linked to Yue Xian's mobile phone number, and thus it could be determined that the copy of the above agreement was sent to Shao Ping by Yue Xian via WeChat.

3. A recording of the telephone conversation between Shao Ping and Yue Xian on December 1, 2015, used to prove that the aforementioned WeChat content was sent to Shao Ping by Yue Xian.

4. A recording of the telephone conversation between Shao Ping and Li Jiang, the manager of Xingtongda Company, on December 1, 2015, used to prove that Li Jiang was a deputy general manager of Kuntong Company and a supervisor of Xingtongda Company, that Luo Haidong, one of the shareholders of Xingtongda Company, was essentially holding shares on behalf of Kuntong Company, that the purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to revitalize Kuntong Company to repay its debts, and that Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company were effectively a personality confusion relationship with one set of personnel and two business licenses.

5. Two lease agreements signed by Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company on July 18, 2009, and September 20, 2009, whereby Kuntong Company leased to Xingtongda Company "11 rooms south of the company's internal yard, 300 square meters of yard, and the second-level stockyard" and "three rooms on the left side of the company's main gate" for use as offices, at an annual rent of 3,000 yuan each. Shao Ping argued that this evidence could prove that the office locations of Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company were the same, and the rent under these leases was abnormally low, and that the two companies achieved the purpose of Kuntong Company operating through Xingtongda Company in this way.

6. The "Measures for Handling Overdue Loans from Pudong Development Bank" issued by Huachengyuan Company to Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company on October 18, 2011. The main content was that Huachengyuan Company had borrowed 14 million yuan from Pudong Development Bank and supplied it to Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company in the form of coke supply. Because the two companies had not repaid, the interest owed by Huachengyuan Company after it borrowed from society was to be repaid by the two companies. Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company confirmed this by affixing their seals. Shao Ping used this to prove that Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company were integrated in actual operations.

Chen Jianming, the legal representative of Xingtongda Company, stated in court that regarding the "Agreed Agreement" between Yue Xian and Kuntong Company, he had reviewed it at the time it was signed, and Luo Haidong, another shareholder of Xingtongda Company, had also signed a similar agreement with Yue Yue, the actual shareholder of Kuntong Company, and Luo Haidong held shares in Xingtongda Company on behalf of Yue Yue. However, Chen Jianming did not retain the originals of either agreement. Furthermore, regarding the evidence provided by Shao Ping and the facts it sought to prove, Chen Jianming stated that it was consistent with the objective facts. The purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to act as a platform for Kuntong Company, enabling Kuntong Company to resume operations through Xingtongda Company. Xingtongda Company had never engaged in any business other than Kuntong Company's actual business operations. All of Xingtongda Company's business activities were conducted in accordance with Kuntong Company's instructions, and the ultimate results were also obtained by Kuntong Company.

This Court holds that during the first instance and the first instance retrial, the Yunnan High People's Court, on the grounds that the 32,568,125.44 yuan creditor's right that Shao Ping had acquired from Huachengyuan Company and the creditor's rights involved in this case did not arise from the same legal relationship, did not examine or determine that part of the claim, while clarifying that Shao Ping could file a separate lawsuit. Since reviewing that part of the claim in the second instance would involve the exercise of the right to defense of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company, as well as the interests of the trial level, the second instance should also not examine it. Shao Ping may file a separate lawsuit.

This Court holds that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Kuntong Company should bear joint and several liability for the debts in question.

First, the content of the "Minutes of the Creditors' Meeting Involving Tonghai Kuntong Industry and Trade Company" formed on June 10, 2009, under the auspices of the Yuxi Intermediate People's Court, shows that because Kuntong Company was sealed up by the court and could hardly continue operations, in order to allow the creditors' claims to be satisfied, Huachengyuan Company cooperated with Kuntong Company. Kuntong Company's assets were handed over to Huachengyuan Company for management, and its external debts were remitted by Huachengyuan Company into the court's account to assist with enforcement. Although Huachengyuan Company and Kuntong Company did not cooperate in accordance with the above meeting minutes afterward, the minutes can prove the fact that Kuntong Company was in a state of being unable to operate due to court enforcement.

Second, from the business registration materials and identity documents, Kuntong Company's legal representative changed to Yue Yue on November 18, 2007. Yue Yue is the son of Yue Xiukuan and Zhang Shufen, the two shareholders of the company. Yue Xian is a supervisor of Kuntong Company, Yang Qionghua is a staff member of Kuntong Company, and Kong Libo is a financial staff member of Kuntong Company. The business registration materials of Xingtongda Company show that Xingtongda Company applied for establishment registration on August 27, 2009. Yue Xian is also a shareholder of Xingtongda Company, Yang Qionghua serves as a supervisor of Xingtongda Company, and Kong Libo also serves as a financial staff member of Xingtongda Company. The above evidence shows that in terms of financial personnel, key staff, and shareholder composition, there was mutual crossover or overlap between Xingtongda Company and Kuntong Company.

Third, the "Agreed Agreement" signed by Yue Xian and Kuntong Company on August 30, 2009, submitted by Shao Ping in the second instance, although a copy in form, can be determined, in light of the WeChat records between Yue Xian and Shao Ping, their telephone conversation recording on December 1, 2015, and Chen Jianming's statement in court, that Yue Xian held shares in Xingtongda Company on behalf of Kuntong Company. This indicates that Kuntong Company effectively held shares in Xingtongda Company through Yue Xian.

Fourth, the two lease agreements signed by Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company on July 18, 2009, and September 20, 2009, can prove that although the parties used the form of lease contracts for Xingtongda Company to rent Kuntong Company's office spaces, yards, and stockyards, from the fact that the agreed rent amounts were abnormally low, it can be seen that the parties actually had mixed office locations, business equipment, and production sites.

Fifth, the content of the "Report on the Production and Operation of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" submitted jointly by Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company to the Tonghai County State Tax Bureau and Xiushan Branch on September 16, 2009, and the "Report on the Causes of Tax Burden of Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company" submitted on October 25, 2011, shows that in 2009, Kuntong Company's tax control device had been seized by the state tax bureau due to overdue taxes. From September 2009, Xingtongda Company purchased raw materials externally and sold them to Kuntong Company, and Kuntong Company's products were sold to Xingtongda Company, which then resold them externally. Xingtongda Company, as "the purchaser of raw materials and auxiliary materials and the seller of products (by-products) for Kuntong Company, does not aim for profit. Therefore, for its procurement and sales to Kuntong Company, it adopts the following methods: 1. Raw materials are purchased and sold at cost; 2. A minimal purchase-sales margin is retained on product sales (to cover Xingtongda Company's daily basic expenses)." The above evidence, combined with the aforementioned "Minutes of the Creditors' Meeting Involving Tonghai Kuntong Industry and Trade Company" formed on June 10, 2009, under the auspices of the Yuxi Intermediate People's Court, shows that Kuntong Company, unable to continue operations due to being sealed up by the people's court and having its tax control device seized by the state tax bureau, and failing to actually perform the above meeting minutes with Huachengyuan Company, then established Xingtongda Company with Chen Jianming, through Yue Xian and Luo Haidong holding shares on its behalf. The purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to restore Kuntong Company's production and operations.

Sixth, in the two Loan Agreements signed between Shao Ping and Xingtongda Company on March 29, 2011, with amounts of RMB 29,200,000 and RMB 17,160,000 respectively, in addition to the signature of Chen Jianming as the legal representative of the lending party Xingtongda Company, the signatures of Yue Yue and Yue Sheng (Yue Yue's brother), the legal representatives of Kuntong Company, also appeared. On the receipt for RMB 4,905,000 issued by Xingtongda Company to Shao Ping on April 18, 2011, in addition to Chen Jianming's signature, Yue Yue also signed the receipt. On the Receipt for RMB 18,895,000 issued by Xingtongda Company to Shao Ping on October 10, 2011, in addition to Chen Jianming's signature, Yue Yue also signed the receipt. The legal significance of the above signatures could be interpreted as that determined by the court of first instance, namely that Yue Yue signed as a witness. Another interpretation, combining the aforementioned facts of the high degree of commingling between Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company in terms of shareholding, financial personnel, office premises, etc., is that when Xingtongda Company entered into the loan agreements with Shao Ping, both parties were fully aware that the purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to realize the operation of Kuntong Company through Xingtongda Company, and that the actual use of the lent funds was also for the restoration of production and operation of Kuntong Company. Therefore, Yue Yue's act of signing the above loan instruments was in fact an act of confirming the loan relationship on behalf of Kuntong Company. This Court is of the opinion that characterizing the legal significance of Yue Yue's signature as an act of witnessing, without other supporting evidence, conflicts with the facts proven by the foregoing series of evidence. Yue Yue's act of signing the aforementioned loan instruments also indicates, from another perspective, a high degree of commingling between Kuntong Company and Xingtongda Company.

Based on a comprehensive assessment of the multiple pieces of evidence above, it can be determined that the purpose of establishing Xingtongda Company was to restore the production and operation of Kuntong Company through Xingtongda Company. Kuntong Company became a shareholder of Xingtongda Company by means of shareholding through persons such as Yue Xian and Luo Haidong. The two companies exhibited a high degree of commingling in terms of financial personnel, working staff, business premises, production and operation, etc. By establishing Xingtongda Company through this method, Kuntong Company utilized the independent legal person status of Xingtongda Company and the limited liability of its shareholders, thereby harming the interests of Shao Ping as a creditor. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Kuntong Company shall assume joint and several liability for the debts borrowed in the name of Xingtongda Company from Shao Ping. Shao Ping's ground of appeal is partially established, and this Court supports it.

In summary, the judgment of first instance failed to make a comprehensive assessment of the multiple pieces of evidence, failed to accurately evaluate the evidence, and made erroneous factual findings. It merely dismissed Shao Ping's request for Kuntong Company to assume joint and several liability on the ground that Xingtongda Company was not an agent of Kuntong Company, which constituted an error in the application of law. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. Revoke the Civil Judgment (2014) Yungao Min Zai Chu Zi No. 1 of the Yunnan High People's Court;

2. Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. shall, within 15 days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally repay to Shao Ping the principal of the loan in the amount of RMB 74,160,000;

3. Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. shall, within 15 days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally pay to Shao Ping interest on the loan principal of RMB 74,160,000 [including: (1) with RMB 34,791,600 as the principal, interest calculated from March 29, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (2) with RMB 4,040,960 as the principal, interest calculated from April 19, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (3) with RMB 2,000,000 as the principal, interest calculated from April 22, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (4) with RMB 800,000 as the principal, interest calculated from April 23, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (5) with RMB 1,900,000 as the principal, interest calculated from September 1, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (6) with RMB 1,000,000 as the principal, interest calculated from September 16, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (7) with RMB 827,440 as the principal, interest calculated from September 17, 2011 to November 7, 2011; (8) with RMB 74,160,000 as the principal, interest calculated from November 8, 2011 until the date of expiry of the performance period specified in this judgment], at the same-period benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China;

3. Dismiss the other claims of Shao Ping.

If the obligation to pay monetary amounts is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with the provisions of Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Court costs of the first instance: RMB 584,310.84, to be borne by Shao Ping in the amount of RMB 178,214.81, and jointly and severally borne by Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 406,096.03. Court costs of the retrial: RMB 584,310.84, to be borne by Shao Ping in the amount of RMB 178,214.81, and jointly and severally borne by Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 406,096.03. Court costs of the appeal: RMB 584,310.84, to be borne by Shao Ping in the amount of RMB 178,214.81, and jointly and severally borne by Yunnan Tonghai Kuntong Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Tonghai Xingtongda Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 406,096.03.

This judgment is final.
